newsitem.title: THAILAND: RESEARCH ALERT - Swedish Motors rated sell.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Swedish Motors rated sell.

text.p: Seamico Securities on Friday recommended investors sell Thai car manufacturer Swedish Motors Corp because of the company's heavy spending on marketing and promotion and overly optimistic projections for 1997 profits.

"The company estimates that 1996 net profit will be roughly half of that recorded in the previous year. This is about right, but its hopes that it will be able to double net profit in 1997 are overly optimistic and carry considerable leeway," Seamico said in a report.
Swedish Motors is Thailand's sole agent for AB Volvo cars and it also provides after sales service and parts.
It has several subsidiaries related to the automotive business, the major ones being Thai Chrysler Automotive and Scandinavian Leasing.
"With two new Volvo models introduced to Thailand in Dec '96 and Chrysler's designs on making inroads into the pickup and minivan segments, marketing expenses will be increasing," Seamico said.
Swedish Motors shares slipped 0.25 baht to 37.25 on Thursday. The stock was untraded by mid-afternoon on Friday.
